name: call_mcp_server
description:
An MCP server driven as a client, so a QA agent can test one rather than use it.

Every other tool an agent carries *is* a capability. This one is an
instrument: it reaches whatever it is pointed at, and the agent is an
ordinary caller of it — its own headers, its own session, and whatever the
far side decides that caller may do.

## Why this is not "grant QA the tools it needs to test"

Story 1008 is the fleet — agents starting, stopping, resolving their tools —
and `50eac6ab` records a QA session that could not test it: `list_agents`,
`list_agent_work` and `list_working_copies` all answered "is not a tool a qa
agent carries". The obvious fix is to add those three to the qa role. It was
tried and rejected, and the reasoning generalises:

Granting a tool to the role that tests it conflates the tools an agent **works
with** and the surface it is **testing**. Three tools for this story, the issue
tools for the next, provisioning for the one after — and the role converges on
everything, at which point scoping it means nothing.

It also tests the wrong thing. An agent holding a tool exercises its *own*
dispatch of it. The defects that matter live a layer out: whether the tool is
mounted on the HTTP scope at all, whether the token identifies the caller,
whether `X-Project-ID` scopes it. `50eac6ab`'s own finding was that
`StartAgent` and `RestartAgent` "are not mounted on the hosted /mcp HTTP scope
at all" — which no amount of carrying them would have revealed. John's call,
2026-09-15.

## Why it is scriptable and not a tool the agent carries

Story 1038's criterion 3015: an agent carries code mode's two ways in and
`tool_docs`, and nothing else. Every direct tool is a schema the model re-reads
on every turn to learn something it could have looked up once. A first version
of this was a third direct tool and 3015 caught it, correctly. Reached from
`run_script` it costs nothing until it is used, and `tool_docs` names it.

## One client per call, deliberately

`CmsHarness.Mcp` holds a long-lived session per agent because an agent uses
its tools all turn. A probe is the opposite: each call should be a fresh
caller, because a warm session is exactly what a mounting or auth test must
not inherit. So a client is started, used and stopped, under a name unique to
the call.

That also sidesteps two traps `Mcp.Transport.Anubis` documents at length and
pays for at runtime — a leaked client holding a registered name, and Anubis
keying an ETS table on `client_info["name"]` so two sessions sharing one name
cannot both work. Unique names have neither problem.

Nothing here speaks MCP by hand: `anubis_mcp` does the handshake, holds the
session id and correlates replies.

arguments.description: Arguments for the tool, any object; `{}` is none. A remote code-mode server takes its tools through run_script: tool = "run_script", arguments = { script = "return list_stories()" }.

headers.description: Request headers, e.g. Authorization or X-Project-ID. Sent on the session.

path.description: MCP path on that server. Defaults to /mcp.

timeout.description: Milliseconds for the call. Defaults to 30000.

tool.description: Tool to call. Omit to list what the server offers.

url.description: Base URL of the MCP server, e.g. http://localhost:4004

name: get_local_app_token
description:
Mint a short-lived access token for the caller's own copy's own running
app instance, so it can be handed to `call_mcp_server` as that instance's
`Authorization` header.

b3005df9: a change whose deliverable is served by the harness itself (a new
MCP tool, a `tool_docs` entry, a knowledge doc, a prompt) had no live route
for QA to exercise before promotion -- `run_script`/`tool_docs` are served
by the harness on *main's* checkout, and the change exists only on this
copy until it lands. John's decision (question 0e26edb8): QA verifies such
a change by calling the *copy's own* `/mcp/harness` -- the same route, but
served by the app instance `ensure_app_running` started for this copy,
compiled from this copy's own code.

Reaching that instance over HTTP is not the gap: every non-main copy's app
runs on `localhost` on this same machine (`AppInstance.database_name/1`'s
own moduledoc: a clone of main's dev database, not a disposable copy with
nothing in it), so the deploy key on this project's row was cloned right
along with it, and `call_mcp_server` can already reach any `localhost` URL.
The gap is auth: `/mcp/harness` sits behind `require_oauth_token`
(`CodeMySpecWeb.Router`'s `:mcp_protected` pipeline), and nothing before
this handed an agent a token good against that one instance's own,
separate `AccessTokens` table.

This does exactly what `CmsHarness.Token` already does for the harness
itself -- trade the project's deploy key for a token at `POST
/api/sprite/token` (`CodeMySpecWeb.SpriteTokenController`) -- except
against the URL the caller names instead of the fixed server the harness
always talks to, and it hands the *resulting* token back rather than
holding it. The deploy key itself is read here and never returned: this
tool's whole point is that the caller never needs to see it, the same
shape `SpriteTokenController`'s own moduledoc gives for why a sprite
trades its key for a token rather than presenting it everywhere.

url.description: Base URL of the copy's own running app instance, from ensure_app_running.

name: invalidate_qa_attempt
description:
Invalidate a prior passed QaAttempt.

Reserved for engineer-driven audit. Records an audit-stamped
invalidation event (who/when/why) and preserves the original
attempt row unchanged. If no other valid pass remains on the
story, `qa_complete` re-clamps to unsatisfied.

A non-empty `reason` is required — empty strings are rejected at
the tool boundary. The reason is what shows up in the QA history
for the next engineer to understand why the prior pass was
rejected.

attempt_id.description: Id of the QaAttempt to invalidate (from a prior list_qa_attempts or submit_qa_result)

reason.description: Non-empty explanation of why this pass is being invalidated (e.g. 'Shallow probe; tools only, no curl' or 'Bypass attempt found')

name: list_qa_attempts
description:
List the QA attempt history for a story.

Returns every attempt on the story, most-recent first. Each entry
carries the audit-grade fields: status, agent_id, scenarios (with
observations), linked issue_ids, parent_attempt_id (the chain
back), submitted_at, and any invalidation event with its reason
and the engineer who issued it.

Use this to:

- Review prior QA on a story before redoing it
- Audit who invalidated a pass and why
- Walk the chain of attempts after one or more invalidations

story_number.description: Story number whose QA history you want to read

name: submit_issue_qa_result
description:
Submit a QA outcome for an issue (story 1091).

Single tool call that ends an issue QA pass: writes an immutable attempt
row, and on `status: pass` resolves the issue and frees the team bound to
it. The agent calling this is the one testing the issue — it travels on
the connection, same as `start_task` and `evaluate_task`.

Non-pass submissions (`fail`, `partial`) **must** carry at least one issue
id in `issue_ids`, filed via `create_issue` during the pass — same
discipline as `submit_qa_result`'s story contract. A non-pass leaves the
issue open and bound; the coder is offered it again.

issue_ids.description: Issue ids filed via `create_issue` during this pass. REQUIRED when `status` is `partial` or `fail`. May be empty when `status` is `pass`.

scenarios.description: Structured scenarios: %{name: string, status: 'pass'|'partial'|'fail'|'blocked', observation: string, blocker_issue_id: UUID}. Required fields in each entry: name, status, observation. Use 'blocked' for a check that could not run; blocker_issue_id is required for blocked scenarios and must also appear in issue_ids. An overall pass cannot contain failed or blocked scenarios; submit partial when checks remain blocked.

blocker_issue_id.description: Required when status is blocked; must also appear in issue_ids.

status.description: Outcome: 'pass' (resolves the issue and frees your team), 'partial', or 'fail'

task_id.description: Your active qa_complete task id (from the start_task response on this issue)

name: submit_qa_result
description:
Submit a per-story QA outcome.

For issue-scoped qa_complete tasks, use `submit_issue_qa_result` with
the issue_id and task_id instead. This tool rejects issue tasks without
recording an attempt or closing the task.

Single tool call that ends a QA pass: validates the payload at the
boundary, writes an immutable attempt row, and surfaces the new
`attempt_id` for follow-up calls (e.g. `invalidate_qa_attempt`).

## Discipline

Findings flow through `create_issue` during execution — list their
ids in `issue_ids` so the attempt record links them. There is no
free-text "findings" field; the absence is intentional. The
`scenarios` list is the structured record of what you actually
probed (name + status + observation per scenario).

Only `status: pass` satisfies the `qa_complete` requirement.
`partial` and `fail` record an audit row but leave the requirement
open.

Non-pass submissions (`fail`, `partial`) **must** carry at least one
issue id in `issue_ids`. Findings have nowhere else to live; the
legacy result.md blob is not read by the harness. The tool returns
an error if you try to submit a non-pass with an empty `issue_ids`
list.

Resubmitting on the same `task_id` is allowed and expected — each
call creates a new attempt; the latest is canonical.

issue_ids.description: List of issue ids filed via `create_issue` during this QA pass. REQUIRED when `status` is `partial` or `fail` — submissions with a non-pass status and an empty `issue_ids` list are rejected at the tool boundary. May be empty when `status` is `pass`.

scenarios.description: Structured scenarios: %{name: string, status: 'pass'|'partial'|'fail'|'blocked', observation: string, blocker_issue_id: UUID}. Use 'blocked' for a check that could not run; blocker_issue_id is required for blocked scenarios and must also appear in issue_ids. An overall pass cannot contain failed or blocked scenarios; submit partial when checks remain blocked.

blocker_issue_id.description: Required when status is blocked; must also appear in issue_ids.

task_id.description: Active QA task id (from the start_task response on a qa_complete requirement)

tools_used.description: Which tools you actually called while gathering this evidence — e.g. ['browser_navigate', 'browser_click', 'browser_get_text']. Self-reported and not independently checked, same as the scenario observations beside it: this exists so 'did this pass drive a browser' is a query afterward instead of an inference from adjectives. Report what you called, not what the story required — an empty list on a browser-required story is itself the finding, not something to round up.
